sections.h2: Where to start with a fast Delray Beach sale
sections.html:
Because Delray Beach lies in Palm Beach County, county offices produce your tax bill and handle deed recording and tax certificates. Three questions drive a quick sale here: the condition of the house, what you owe on it, and where the property tax calendar stands.

The city describes its growth from a small farming village into a community of nearly 70,000 residents, built around a historic downtown on Atlantic Avenue. Homes close to downtown are older and may carry deferred upkeep. Newer parts of town usually need less. Financed buyers may want repairs; cash buyers frequently accept the property exactly as it stands.

  • An agent listing suits an owner who can sit through showings and a lender's schedule.
  • An as-is cash sale answers pressure from repairs, a move date or a tax deadline.
  • A renovator is the likelier buyer when the work would scare off a mortgage lender.

Linton was the first name. After crop freezes and a land payment default it became Delray in 1898, and it took the name Delray Beach when two municipalities merged on May 11, 1927. Land west of the canal had incorporated in 1911, and land east of the Intracoastal in 1923.

The mainland and barrier island halves still feel different: beachside living east of the waterway, inland neighborhoods to the west. A bridge across the canal first linked them in 1911. Homes vary enormously in age and in condition, and on an older parcel a long ownership chain can hide a mortgage nobody formally released. Have your title company look for stale easements and unreleased liens.

Downtown centers on Old School Square and Atlantic Avenue, and buyers who like that setting often shop within walking distance. The 1913 school building is now the Cornell Museum of Art and History, while the 1925 high school is the Crest Theatre.

Does your house stand in or beside a historic area? Planning staff can tell you what rules govern exterior changes, and renovation-minded buyers will want that answer before they commit.

More than 600,000 bills go out from the county tax collector by November 1. You can pay from that date through March 31, after which the tax is delinquent and carries penalties and interest. The appraiser's Notice of Proposed Taxes arrives each August.

Discount by payment month
Payment monthDiscount
November4 percent off
December3 percent off
January2 percent off
February1 percent off
MarchFull amount, no discount
  • Florida law pushes a weekend or holiday due date to the next working day.
  • No online payment is possible for delinquent tax, and a postmark does not count as proof that you paid.
  • If the house has sold but the bill still came to you, a Property Sold Form from the tax collector sends it to the right person.

The county's property tax page describes an installment plan and a homestead tax deferral. Phone the collector before listing to see whether either applies to you.

The state's deed tax runs 70 cents for each $100 of consideration (section 201.02). Everyone on the deed is liable regardless of who agreed to pay it. Miami-Dade stands apart with a rate of its own, but Palm Beach County does not, so the standard figure applies here.

Under section 28.24 the clerk may bill $5.00 for page one and $4.00 for each page after, plus trust fund and technology charges. Two deeds are listed as exempt: a spousal homestead deed where a mortgage is the only consideration, and a divorce deed covering the marital home.

Some older owners use lady bird deeds. In October 2020 a Department of Revenue advisement found that a particular one owed no documentary stamp tax, since the life tenants kept full powers. Because it turns on its own facts, have a title attorney look at yours first.

Three yardsticks help: what you net, how long closing takes, and how likely the deal is to collapse. A listing brings in more buyers but also showings, an appraisal and loan conditions. Selling for cash lets you pick the closing date and usually removes repair requests.

  1. Obtain a written mortgage payoff.
  2. Find out if this year's property taxes have been paid.
  3. Learn from each buyer who covers stamps, title and recording.
  4. Request the closing statement before the day itself.

If a foreclosure is under way, the clerk's sale is held 20 to 35 days after final judgment unless the plaintiff gives more time.

Portability is the tool. Start a new Florida homestead inside three years of January 1 of the year you gave up the old one, and the Save Our Homes difference may reduce what the new house is assessed at. Both Form DR-501T and Form DR-501 are due March 1.

You lose homestead by renting the property, by moving out permanently, or by ceasing to be a Florida resident. An extra exemption may be available to owners 65 and older where local ordinance provides one and income is under the limit, so the county appraiser can tell you if Delray Beach has it.

When you accept an offer, the title company searches the records, writes the deed and agrees a date with you. Take photo ID, keys and any garage or gate openers. Read every line of the settlement statement, and check how the money will reach you. Your lender gets paid first, taxes are prorated, and you receive the rest after recording.

It helps to pack and clear the house before closing, and to photograph its condition on the day you hand over keys. Switch utilities only on the agreed date, and keep your own insurance running until the deed is recorded.

A folder of records speeds everything, and it keeps surprises from showing up late in the process. Include the deed, your most recent mortgage statement, the most recent tax bill, any permit paperwork and warranties for the roof or appliances. Write down known problems with the house and the dates of past repairs, because buyers and inspectors ask about them. If several people own the house, make sure each one will be available to sign, or arrange a signing for those who live elsewhere. Heirs and co-owners in particular should agree in advance on the asking price, the lowest offer they will take and who speaks for the group when a buyer calls. Put that agreement in writing so nobody has to guess later.

Retain a copy of every page. A seller who is also buying should request closing figures early, so the next lender has what it needs.

faqs.q: When did Delray Beach become a city?
faqs.a: The City of Delray Beach was formed on May 11, 1927, when the Town of Delray Beach and the City of Delray united. They had been incorporated separately, in 1923 and 1911.

faqs.q: What was Delray Beach called before?
faqs.a: It started as Linton, named in 1895 for a congressman in the settlement group. Residents changed it to Delray in 1898 after freezes damaged crops.

faqs.q: When are Palm Beach County property taxes delinquent?
faqs.a: April 1. Bills are payable from November 1 through March 31, and delinquent taxes cannot be paid online.

faqs.q: Is there an early payment discount in Palm Beach County?
faqs.a: Yes: 4 percent in November, 3 percent in December, 2 percent in January and 1 percent in February, with none in March.

faqs.q: Do I pay documentary stamp tax when I sell in Delray Beach?
faqs.a: The contract decides who pays, but all parties are liable. The statewide deed rate is 70 cents per $100 of consideration.
